acceptance: A TimeoutExpired from any local git subprocess used by reads and mutations reaches the caller as an ok:false envelope with a code, never as a raw exception; for a mutation the message states whether anything was pushed
A timeout does not trigger a rebuild of the local object store
A test injects the timeout into each local git subcommand listed in the description for list_items, show_item and a mutation
context:
Imported on 2026-10-28 from the BenchBox tracker item(s): todo-db-git-backend-checkout-timeout-resilience. Those items stay open in BenchBox to track the dependency.

Source context (todo-db-git-backend-checkout-timeout-resilience): Discovered during batch comment cleanup closeout when git checkout FETCH_HEAD or checkout --detach tip timed out under HTTPS fetch burst pressure.

Still present 2026-10-17 in the vendored wheel BenchBox uses (_project/scripts/vendor/todo_db-0.9.1-py3-none-any.whl): todo_db/git_backend.py:398 (`checkout --detach tip` in the mutation path) and :630 (`checkout FETCH_HEAD` in the read path) call _git (lines 189-197, timeout GIT_TIMEOUT_S=60 at line 68) without catching TimeoutExpired, while the fetch calls at 240-242 and 375-378 do. Seen six times in one site-split session on 2026-10-17, each surfacing as a raw tool error rather than E_OFFLINE: take ("Command '['git', 'checkout', '--quiet', '--detach', '399fdae8...']' timed out after 60 seconds" at 13:09Z and 'd4a38d3b...' at 21:14Z), update_item ('40489f91...' twice, 21:07Z and 21:09Z), and show_item (checkout FETCH_HEAD, 21:03Z and 21:05Z). Host load was about 5. Each retry succeeded, but the caller could not tell whether a mutation had applied.

REVIEW 2026-10-28 against todo-db 0.10.1 (main d85cdf3), per the todo review checklist and review-protocol L2/L3. VERDICT: VALID, re-scoped, low priority. The 0.9.1 checkout call sites cited in the BenchBox item do not exist in 0.10.1. Evidence for the remaining gap: a fault-injection probe over the Store's local git subcommands (script not kept; the test in this item replaces it) produced RAW TimeoutExpired for every local subcommand listed and coded envelopes only for fetch (E_OFFLINE), push (E_UNKNOWN) and rev-parse on the remote path. Not changed: network timeouts, which are already handled and tested in tests/test_git_pub.py.
description: The reported mechanism no longer exists: 0.10.0 replaced the working-tree checkouts with a bare object store, and fetch, push and ls-remote timeouts already map to E_OFFLINE or E_UNKNOWN. The defect class remains. Injecting subprocess.TimeoutExpired into one local git call at a time (cat-file, commit-tree, hash-object, log, ls-tree, merge-base, read-tree, update-index, update-ref, write-tree) makes list_items, show_item, create_item and take raise the raw exception instead of returning a coded envelope. Local git calls rarely time out, so the likelihood is low; there is no real 0.10.1 incident.
